correctness.rationale: For all v≥4 and a>0, the explicit free 2-convex norm equals an unrestricted semidefinite design optimum; dualization yields the maximum trace of a positive matrix square root. Symmetric-group averaging and the exact two Johnson/Kneser Laplacian eigenspaces reduce the global problem to a strictly concave scalar function. Endpoint derivative conditions yield two sharp thresholds (the second absent at v=4); weighted Cauchy–Schwarz solves the unique interior optimum and the endpoint formulas. Distinct off-diagonal entries of the information matrix recover every positive-amplitude edge weight, proving full uniqueness. Supporting script output: five exact integer spectra, 89 direct spectral comparisons, 15 randomized noninvariant simplex optimizations. Finite computations corroborate the all-parameter proof and are not the proof. The arbitrary-chord criterion follows from the derivative test and global concavity. All limits are expansions of explicit radicals.

value.rationale: The exact two-summing norm is a natural operator-ideal quantity associated with a widely studied Johnson graph. Its complete continuous-amplitude classification produces two nontrivial support transitions, a sharp dimension-four disconnected-complement exception, simultaneous norm screening of arbitrarily many nonuniform disjoint pairs, and distinct 1/v versus 1/v² approach rates of the two boundaries. This supplies structure not implied by a generic convex optimization formula or the known unweighted endpoints.
